TextBlock.TextLine: Fig. 213. Directions of the Compass. tiˊrkɪ-reˊiᵋ or têrk-amêčaˊtyêᵋ (“sun has come in” or “sun has gone out of sight”). aᵋčoˊpta (“it is still day”). em-g̣iˊthilɪ-neˊlyi (“twilight has come”). g̣itg̣iluweˊtyiᵋ (“twilight has become narrow”). g̣êˊthêlu-waiñeˊeᵋ (“twilight has been extinguished”). aiˊvêčha (“in the evening”) or tun-nɪkiruˊiᵋ (“night recently came”). em-g̣ɪnuˊn-nɪkiˊtä neˊlyiᵋ (“midnight has come”). em-g̣ɪnuˊn-nɪkiˊtä halaˊêᵋ (“midnight has passed by”). eimeˊwkwiᵋ (“[dawn] has approached”). ɪˊprɪñg̣êᵋ (“[light] has burst forth”). tñeˊiᵋ (“it has dawned”) or tñaˊɪrg̣ɪn (“morning-dawn”). totɪntoˊêᵋ (“darkness has gone”). tañ-ɪrg̣ɪroˊêᵋ (“it has well dawned”). tirk-iiniˊɪᵋ (“sun has risen”). têˊrkɪ-g̣ɪrg̣olaˊtyêᵋ (“sun has ascended”). tiˊrkɪ-keulkeˊtyiᵋ (“sun has climbed [towards the top]”). am-gɪnoˊt-aᵋloˊwtɪ tɪleˊhtɪ neˊlyiᵋ (“to the mid-day it has gradually approached”). am-gɪnoˊt-aᵋloˊ neˊlyiᵋ (“mid-day has come”). am-gɪnoˊt-aᵋloˊ halaˊêᵋ (“mid-day has passed by”). t-arkɪčhaweˊtɪ neˊlyɪᵋ (“sun descending has come”). t-arkɪčhaˊwkwê or tirk-iwtɪtviˊiᵋ (“sun has descended” or “sun has become low”).
